account: It is ten o'clock on day 1, and I am at the mill for my scheduled grain inspection. No one has yet identified who oversees the grain or reported a specific storage problem. Townsfolk 11 has repeated an unusual, vague report of a 'bridge_or_port_change' at the bakery, mentioning the baker and, in one version, my neighbour. They also say the baker carried a sack of bread there. I cannot tell what change occurred, whether these reports describe one event, or what it was for. A baker carrying bread is not by itself suspicious; I should seek a direct explanation before drawing conclusions. My neighbour said Freight was wondering when to expect my mill visit and would be at the east landing this morning, which may simply concern ordinary grain or transport business. Separately, Builder is undertaking an authorized two-emerald inspection of town hall doors, bridge decking, and the east ferry landing, with written findings due at my office at sixteen thirty. His preliminary report found no visible bridge defects and a normally functioning entrance door. No repairs are authorized. The secretary agreed to transcribe his findings, and I handed over an emerald for a writable office book, although a later request for that emerald suggests some confusion that remains to be clarified. Today's remaining appointments are lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen, tea at my neighbour's east-dock cottage at fifteen, and Builder's office review at sixteen thirty. At present I have no verified evidence of a transport disruption or improper activity.
